$schema_purpose: Deterministic, hard-constraint CSV output format for rdlc-mock-data-generator. Every value here is a strict compliance requirement. Pair with references/gold-example/ for a visual reference.
quoting: RFC 4180 — quote any field containing a comma, double-quote, or line break; escape embedded double-quotes by doubling them

file_naming.rule: Must exactly match the Technical Name given for that table in the confirmed Table Definitions document — this is what the Power BI M/Import partition query will reference as its source file.

header_row.content: Technical Names only, in the exact same order as listed in the confirmed Table Definitions document's column table
header_row.reason: CSV is an ETL/source-layer artifact (maps to TMDL sourceColumn); Business Names are applied later, inside the semantic model layer, not in the source file.

value_conventions.integer_keys: Plain integers, no leading zeros unless the confirmed Type is explicitly a fixed-width string code
value_conventions.boolean_or_flag_columns: Integer 0/1, matching the confirmed column Type (e.g., Int64) — never 'TRUE'/'FALSE' or 'Yes'/'No' string literals
value_conventions.null_representation: Empty string (two consecutive delimiters) — never the literal text 'NULL' or 'N/A'
value_conventions.decimal_separator: Period only; no thousands separators inside any CSV value
value_conventions.text_fields: No leading/trailing whitespace; quote if the value itself contains the delimiter

column_order_rule: Must match the confirmed Table Definitions document's Technical Name column order exactly, left to right.

verification_step.instruction: After generating all CSVs, re-parse each file and confirm: (1) header matches expected Technical Names in order, (2) every fact-table foreign key value exists in its corresponding dimension file, (3) no unexpected null/blank in a required column.
